+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "attribute,expected",
+        [
+            ("MICROBATCH", "microbatch"),
+            ("LAYER", "layer"),
+            ("COMMUNICATION", "communication"),
+            ("ACTIVATION_OFFLOAD", "activation_offload"),

+            ("TRACE_REGION", "trace_region"),
+            ("INFERENCE", "inference"),
+        ],

+    def test_group_name(self, attribute, expected):
+        assert getattr(MegatronSpanGroup, attribute) == expected
+
+    def test_group_names_are_unique(self):
+        assert len(MEGATRON_ONLY_GROUPS) == 8
+
+    def test_megatron_groups_do_not_collide_with_base_groups(self):
+        assert not (MEGATRON_ONLY_GROUPS & SpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS)

+    def test_inherits_base_groups(self):
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.JOB == SpanGroup.JOB
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.CHECKPOINT == SpanGroup.CHECKPOINT
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.STEP == SpanGroup.STEP
+
+
+class TestAllGroups:
+    def test_is_a_frozenset(self):
+        assert isinstance(MegatronSpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS, frozenset)
+
+    def test_extends_base_all_groups(self):
+        assert SpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS <= MegatronSpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS
+
+    def test_contains_every_megatron_group(self):
+        assert MEGATRON_ONLY_GROUPS <= MegatronSpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS
+
+    def test_is_exactly_base_plus_megatron(self):
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS == SpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS | MEGATRON_ONLY_GROUPS
+
+
+class TestPresets:
+    """Presets must nest: default subset of per_step subset of all."""
+
+    def test_expected_presets_exist(self):
+        assert set(MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS) == {"default", "per_step", "profiling", "all"}
+
+    def test_every_preset_is_a_subset_of_all_groups(self):
+        for name, groups in MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS.items():
+            assert groups <= MegatronSpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS, f"preset {name!r} has unknown groups"
+
+    def test_default_is_a_subset_of_per_step(self):
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["default"] <= MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["per_step"]
+
+    def test_all_and_profiling_are_every_group(self):
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["all"] == MegatronSpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["profiling"] == MegatronSpanGroup.ALL_GROUPS
+
+    def test_default_is_coarse_grained(self):
+        """`default` is the production preset; it must not carry per-step cost."""
+        default = MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["default"]
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.JOB in default
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.CHECKPOINT in default
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.EVALUATE in default
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.FIRST_ITERATION in default
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.INFERENCE in default
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.STEP not in default
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.FORWARD_BACKWARD not in default
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.MICROBATCH not in default
+
+    def test_per_step_adds_step_level_groups(self):
+        per_step = MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["per_step"]
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.STEP in per_step
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.FORWARD_BACKWARD in per_step
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.OPTIMIZER in per_step
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.MODEL_INIT in per_step
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.LOAD_CHECKPOINT in per_step
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.COMMUNICATION in per_step
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup.DATA_LOADING in per_step
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "group",
+        [
+            MegatronSpanGroup.MICROBATCH,
+            MegatronSpanGroup.LAYER,
+            MegatronSpanGroup.ACTIVATION_OFFLOAD,
+            MegatronSpanGroup.TRACE_REGION,
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_verbose_groups_are_opt_in_only(self, group):

+        assert group not in MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["per_step"]
+        assert group in MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS["all"]
+
+    def test_presets_do_not_shadow_the_base_class(self):
+        """Subclassing must not leave MegatronSpanGroup resolving base presets."""
+        assert MegatronSpanGroup._PRESETS is not SpanGroup._PRESETS
+
+
+class TestResolve:
+    @pytest.mark.skipif(HAVE_NEMO_LENS, reason="stub SpanGroup is only used without nemo-lens")
+    def test_resolve_without_nemo_lens_raises(self):

+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(HAVE_NEMO_LENS, reason="stub SpanGroup is only used without nemo-lens")
+class TestStubFallback:

+                "evaluate",
+                "model_init",
+                "load_checkpoint",
+                "step",
+                "forward_backward",
+                "optimizer",

+"""Unit tests for ``megatron.core.telemetry.training_metrics``.
+

+OTel ``MeterProvider``, so they need neither ``opentelemetry`` nor ``nemo-lens``
+and they can assert exactly which instrument received which value.
+"""

+
+import pytest

+from megatron.core.telemetry import training_metrics
+from megatron.core.telemetry.training_metrics import record_training_metrics
+
+# Argument name -> (instrument kind, exported metric name).

+    "step_duration_ms": ("histogram", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_STEP_DURATION_MS),
+    "loss": ("gauge", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_LOSS),
+    "throughput_tflops": ("gauge", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_THROUGHPUT_TFLOPS),
+    "grad_norm": ("gauge", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_GRAD_NORM),
+    "skipped_iters": ("counter", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_SKIPPED_ITERS),
+    "learning_rate": ("gauge", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_LEARNING_RATE),
+    "tokens_per_sec": ("gauge", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_TOKENS_PER_SEC),
+    "memory_allocated_gb": ("gauge", training_metrics.MEGATRON_TRAINING_MEMORY_ALLOCATED_GB),
+}
+
+
+class FakeInstrument:
+    """Accepts all three OTel write calls and remembers what it was given."""
+
+    def __init__(self, kind, name):
+        self.kind = kind
+        self.name = name
+        self.values = []
+
+    def record(self, value):
+        self.values.append(value)
+
+    def set(self, value):
+        self.values.append(value)
+
+    def add(self, value):
+        self.values.append(value)
+
+
+class FakeMeter:
+    """Stands in for an OTel ``Meter``; must be weak-referenceable."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.instruments = {}
+        self.create_calls = 0
+
+    def _create(self, kind, name):
+        self.create_calls += 1
+        instrument = FakeInstrument(kind, name)
+        self.instruments[name] = instrument
+        return instrument
+
+    def create_histogram(self, name, unit=None, description=None):
+        return self._create("histogram", name)
+
+    def create_gauge(self, name, unit=None, description=None):
+        return self._create("gauge", name)
+
+    def create_counter(self, name, unit=None, description=None):
+        return self._create("counter", name)
+
+
+class BrokenMeter:
+    """Every instrument factory raises, as an SDK misconfiguration would."""
+
+    def create_histogram(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        raise RuntimeError("meter is broken")
+
+    create_gauge = create_histogram
+    create_counter = create_histogram
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def clear_instrument_cache():
+    """The instrument cache is module-global; keep tests independent."""
+    training_metrics._TRAINING_INSTRUMENTS.clear()
+    yield
+    training_metrics._TRAINING_INSTRUMENTS.clear()
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def otel_available(monkeypatch):
+    """Exercise the recording path even when ``opentelemetry`` is absent."""
+    if training_metrics.metrics is None:
+        monkeypatch.setattr(training_metrics, "metrics", object())
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def meter():
+    return FakeMeter()
+
+
+class TestMetricNames:
+    """These strings are the queryable metric names; changing one is breaking."""
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("kind_and_name", INSTRUMENTS.values(), ids=list(INSTRUMENTS))
+    def test_name_is_namespaced(self, kind_and_name):
+        _, name = kind_and_name
+        assert name.startswith("megatron.training.")
+
+    def test_names_are_unique(self):
+        names = [name for _, name in INSTRUMENTS.values()]
+        assert len(set(names)) == len(names)
+
+
+class TestInstrumentCreation:
+    def test_creates_every_instrument_with_the_right_kind(self, meter):
+        record_training_metrics(meter, loss=1.0)
+
+        for kind, name in INSTRUMENTS.values():
+            assert name in meter.instruments, f"{name} was never created"
+            assert meter.instruments[name].kind == kind

+    def test_creates_exactly_the_expected_instruments(self, meter):
+        record_training_metrics(meter, loss=1.0)
+
+        assert set(meter.instruments) == {name for _, name in INSTRUMENTS.values()}
+
+    def test_instruments_are_created_once_per_meter(self, meter):
+        record_training_metrics(meter, loss=1.0)
+        creates_after_first_call = meter.create_calls

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("E", [2, 4, 8])
+def test_grouped_gemm_split_invariance(E):
+    """Splitting the M dimension at expert boundaries must give bitwise-identical
+    output to the full call."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    K, N = 128, 96
+    # Build expert-grouped tokens: 32 tokens per expert
+    per_expert = 32
+    M = per_expert * E
+    x = torch.randn(M, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = torch.randn(E, N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    m_indices = torch.repeat_interleave(
+        torch.arange(E, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32),
+        torch.tensor([per_expert] * E, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32),
+    ).contiguous()
+
+    counts = [per_expert] * E
+    y_full = _bf16_grouped_gemm_contiguous(x, w, m_indices, counts)
+
+    # Split into halves at expert boundaries (mid-expert split is not legal for
+    # contiguous-layout DeepGEMM — must split on a boundary).
+    half = (E // 2) * per_expert
+    y0 = _bf16_grouped_gemm_contiguous(
+        x[:half].contiguous(), w, m_indices[:half].contiguous(), counts[: E // 2] + [0] * (E // 2)
+    )
+    y1 = _bf16_grouped_gemm_contiguous(
+        x[half:].contiguous(), w, m_indices[half:].contiguous(), [0] * (E // 2) + counts[E // 2 :]
+    )
+    y_cat = torch.cat([y0, y1], dim=0)
+    assert torch.equal(
+        y_full, y_cat

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""CUDA memory regression test for MoE full recompute activation cleanup.
+
+Verifies that explicit deletion of intermediate tensors in unpermute()
+reduces peak CUDA memory during full recomputation.
+
+Issue: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/3221
+PR:    https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/5197
+"""
+
+import gc
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+
+def unpermute_without_del(
+    permuted_tokens: torch.Tensor, sorted_indices: torch.Tensor, restore_shape: torch.Size
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Original unpermute WITHOUT the explicit del statements (baseline)."""
+    _, hidden = restore_shape
+    input_dtype = permuted_tokens.dtype
+    output_tokens = torch.zeros(
+        restore_shape, dtype=permuted_tokens.dtype, device=permuted_tokens.device
+    )
+    output_tokens.scatter_add_(0, sorted_indices.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, hidden), permuted_tokens)
+    out = output_tokens.to(dtype=input_dtype)
+    return out
+
+
+def unpermute_with_del(
+    permuted_tokens: torch.Tensor, sorted_indices: torch.Tensor, restore_shape: torch.Size
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Fixed unpermute WITH explicit del (the PR's approach)."""
+    _, hidden = restore_shape
+    input_dtype = permuted_tokens.dtype
+    output_tokens = torch.zeros(
+        restore_shape, dtype=permuted_tokens.dtype, device=permuted_tokens.device
+    )
+    output_tokens.scatter_add_(0, sorted_indices.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, hidden), permuted_tokens)
+    out = output_tokens.to(dtype=input_dtype)
+    # Explicitly release intermediate tensor references so CUDA allocator
+    # can reclaim memory immediately during full recomputation.
+    del output_tokens, permuted_tokens, sorted_indices
+    return out
+
+
+class MoELayer(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Minimal MoE layer wrapper for recompute memory testing."""
+
+    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, ffn_hidden: int, unpermute_fn):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.ffn = torch.nn.Sequential(
+            torch.nn.Linear(hidden_size, ffn_hidden),
+            torch.nn.GELU(),
+            torch.nn.Linear(ffn_hidden, hidden_size),
+        )
+        self.unpermute_fn = unpermute_fn
+
+    def forward(
+        self, permuted_tokens: torch.Tensor, sorted_indices: torch.Tensor, restore_shape: torch.Size
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        expert_out = self.ffn(permuted_tokens)
+        return self.unpermute_fn(expert_out, sorted_indices, restore_shape)
+
+
+def measure_peak_memory(fn, *args, **kwargs):
+    """Run fn with CUDA memory tracking and return (result, peak_allocated, retained_after)."""
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+    gc.collect()
+    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    result = fn(*args, **kwargs)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    peak_mb = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**2
+    retained_mb = torch.cuda.memory_allocated() / 1024**2
+    return result, peak_mb, retained_mb
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA not available")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_permuted_tokens, num_total_tokens, hidden_size, ffn_hidden",
+    [
+        (65536, 131072, 4096, 14336),  # DeepSeek-V3 scale
+        (32768, 65536, 2048, 7168),  # Medium scale
+        (16384, 32768, 1024, 4096),  # Small scale
+    ],
+)
+def test_moe_recompute_memory_reduction(
+    num_permuted_tokens, num_total_tokens, hidden_size, ffn_hidden
+):
+    """Verify del statements reduce peak CUDA memory in full recompute mode.
+
+    The test simulates MoE's token permutation pattern: tokens are first
+    permuted (grouped by expert), fed through FFN, then unpermuted back
+    to original token order via scatter_add_. In full recompute mode,
+    the forward pass runs again during backward, and intermediate tensors
+    from scatter_add_ can accumulate if not explicitly freed.
+    """
+
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    restore_shape = torch.Size((num_total_tokens, hidden_size))
+
+    def build_inputs():
+        # Fresh tensors per measurement so grads from the other path do not leak.
+        permuted_tokens = torch.randn(
+            num_permuted_tokens, hidden_size, device=device, dtype=dtype, requires_grad=True
+        )
+        sorted_indices = torch.randint(0, num_total_tokens, (num_permuted_tokens,), device=device)
+        target = torch.randn(num_total_tokens, hidden_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)

**[SUGGESTION Simplification]** The new `use_layer_wise_param_layout` argument is accepted but never read, and its default of `True` contradicts the layout dev actually applies.

**Failure.**
- `_ddp_wrap` picks the layout function only from `use_layer_wise_distributed_optimizer` (L321-330).
- `compute_full_param_layout` then picks padded or compact from `ddp_config.use_layer_wise_param_layout`. That field defaults to `False` (compact) in `DistributedDataParallelConfig`, and [`arguments.py` L2028-2029](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4236407f9d6f3e66dee178e57a1f701be00cd33c/megatron/training/arguments.py#L2028-L2029) calls compact "the default".
- So `build_distributed_models(..., use_layer_wise_param_layout=True)` and `...=False` give identical layouts. The same is true for `unimodal_build_distributed_models` and `prepare_existing_model_chunks_for_distributed_training`.
- On main, #6286 makes this argument select the padded layout. A caller ported from main therefore silently gets the compact layout instead.
- Callers that skip `arguments.py`, such as the MIMO builder or anyone using ModelBuilder directly, also skip the compact-layout checks that are keyed on the `ddp_config` flag (`num_distributed_optimizer_instances == 1` and the fp8 restrictions).

The argument is new in this PR and is only passed along, never used. It appears at [base.py L237](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4236407f9d6f3e66dee178e57a1f701be00cd33c/megatron/training/models/base.py#L237), [dist_utils.py L57/L148/L285](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4236407f9d6f3e66dee178e57a1f701be00cd33c/megatron/training/models/dist_utils.py#L57) and [examples/mimo/training/builder.py L126](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4236407f9d6f3e66dee178e57a1f701be00cd33c/examples/mimo/training/builder.py#L126). The docstrings call it a compatibility shim for main's API, but nothing marks it as temporary.

**Correction.** `ddp_config.use_layer_wise_param_layout` should stay the only thing that selects the layout, and the extra argument should never silently disagree with it. Either option works:
- **(a)** Change the default to `None` in all five signatures, and add this check in `_ddp_wrap`:
  ```python
  if (
      use_layer_wise_param_layout is not None
      and use_layer_wise_param_layout != ddp_config.use_layer_wise_param_layout
  ):
      raise ValueError(
          "use_layer_wise_param_layout is ignored on this branch; set "
          "DistributedDataParallelConfig.use_layer_wise_param_layout instead."
      )
  ```
  Use `warnings.warn` instead of raising if callers need a softer transition.
- **(b)** At minimum, add a `TODO` or deprecation note to the docstrings saying the value is ignored and will be removed once main selects the layout from `ddp_config`. Also change the misleading `True` default to `None`.

Before changing any defaults, search `tests/unit_tests/training` for tests that assert the value passed along. I did not check this.

**Preservation.**
- Keep the argument in all signatures, so callers written against main do not hit a `TypeError`.
- Keep the current `training.py` call, which leaves the argument out; dev's plumbing test asserts that exact call.
- Keep layout selection from `ddp_config` unchanged for both the compact default and the padded layout (`--use-layer-wise-param-layout`).

**Acceptance.**
- *Proposed test, mismatch case:* call `_ddp_wrap` or `unimodal_build_distributed_models` with `ddp_config.use_layer_wise_param_layout=False`, `use_layer_wise_distributed_optimizer=True`, and an explicit `use_layer_wise_param_layout=True`. Under option (a) this raises (or warns).
- *Proposed test, preservation case:* leaving the argument out, or passing a value that matches `ddp_config`, produces the same `full_param_layout` as today.
- *Static check:* after the change, every use of the argument in `dist_utils.py` is either passing it along or the consistency check.

**[IMPORTANT Compatibility]** `get_vision_model_config` changed signature, but its only in-tree caller was not updated, so the multimodal example now crashes while building the model.

**Failure.**
- This sync brings in main #6332, which changes the signature:
  - before: `get_vision_model_config(config, apply_query_key_layer_scaling)` ([base L179](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ae63ce48d2f0044170d828f658c3dd29dd0e4c98/examples/multimodal/config.py#L179))
  - after: `get_vision_model_config(config, enable_fusions=False)` (this line)
- The caller is [`examples/multimodal/model.py` L132-L134](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/43e8ded904b839caeb60681bcf3ff7b506ffd477/examples/multimodal/model.py#L132-L134). It is not in this PR and is identical to base. It still calls `get_vision_model_config(vision_config, apply_query_key_layer_scaling=args.apply_query_key_layer_scaling)`.
- **Trigger:** any `examples/multimodal/train.py` run. `train.py` imports `model_provider` from `model` ([train.py L17](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/43e8ded904b839caeb60681bcf3ff7b506ffd477/examples/multimodal/train.py#L17)), for example via `pretrain_mistral_clip.sh`.
- **Actual:** `model_provider` raises `TypeError: get_vision_model_config() got an unexpected keyword argument 'apply_query_key_layer_scaling'` before any module is built.
- **Expected:** the vision config is built as it was on dev.
- **Why CI is green:** the `multimodal-llava` functional recipe runs top-level `pretrain_vlm.py` ([recipe L58](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/43e8ded904b839caeb60681bcf3ff7b506ffd477/tests/test_utils/recipes/h100/multimodal-llava.yaml#L58)), not this example.

**Correction.** Keep this file as main has it, and update the caller in `model_provider` (`examples/multimodal/model.py` L131-L134):
```python
    vision_config = deepcopy(base_config)
    vision_config = get_vision_model_config(vision_config)
    # get_vision_model_config now hardcodes False; keep honoring --apply-query-key-layer-scaling.
    vision_config.apply_query_key_layer_scaling = args.apply_query_key_layer_scaling
```
- **Invariant to restore:**
  - Every in-tree call to `get_vision_model_config` matches its signature.
  - The vision config's `apply_query_key_layer_scaling` still follows the CLI flag, as it did on dev.
- **Main may need the same fix.** I could not see main from here. If main's `model.py` has the same stale call, fix it on main too, so the next sync does not bring the mismatch back.

**Preservation.**
- **Fusions:** leaving `enable_fusions` at its default `False` keeps dev's vision fusion settings. `bias_activation_fusion`, `bias_dropout_fusion` and `apply_rope_fusion` stay `False`.
- **`hf://` vision branch:** this branch never set `apply_query_key_layer_scaling`; it inherited the args value through `base_config`. Assigning after the call gives the same result.
- **Other calls:** `get_language_model_config(language_config)` and `get_vision_projection_config(vision_projection_config, hidden_size)` are still compatible and should stay unchanged.

**Acceptance.**
- *Static check:* `model.py` passes no keyword to `get_vision_model_config` that is missing from its signature.
- *Proposed smoke test:* a one-iteration run of `examples/multimodal/train.py` (for example `pretrain_mistral_clip.sh` with `--train-iters 1`) gets past `model_provider` without a `TypeError`.
- *Preservation check:* with `--apply-query-key-layer-scaling`, `vision_config.apply_query_key_layer_scaling` is `True`. Without the flag it is `False`, as on dev.

**[SUGGESTION Simplification]** `--enable-fusions` and `--optimize-broadcast` are `store_true` with `default=True`, so they can never be `False`. Most of the flags #6332 adds, and the new `enable_fusions` parameters in `config.py`, have no reader on dev.

**[SUGGESTION Simplification]** `--enable-fusions` and `--optimize-broadcast` can never be turned off, and nothing reads them. The `enable_fusions` parameters they would feed are never passed, so every fusion is forced off. This is unresolved from review 5488746518.

**Failure**
- **Always on.** `action="store_true", default=True` (L210, L213) makes `args.enable_fusions` and `args.optimize_broadcast` always `True`. No CLI spelling yields `False`.
- **No reader.** None of these calls passes `enable_fusions`, so each config function always takes its `enable_fusions=False` default:
  - [`model.py` L101](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ef8d0901e9925f7abed0bdec14340052850172ea/examples/multimodal/model.py#L101) calls `get_language_model_config(language_config)`.
  - [L132](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ef8d0901e9925f7abed0bdec14340052850172ea/examples/multimodal/model.py#L132) calls `get_vision_model_config(vision_config)`.
  - [L176-L178](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ef8d0901e9925f7abed0bdec14340052850172ea/examples/multimodal/model.py#L176-L178) calls `get_vision_projection_config(...)`.
- **Result.** The flag advertises "Enable fusions in the model", but fusions are always off.
- **Rope fusion side effect.** [`config.py` L9-L14](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ef8d0901e9925f7abed0bdec14340052850172ea/examples/multimodal/config.py#L9-L14) now sets `config.apply_rope_fusion = enable_fusions` for every language branch.
  - On dev, `nemotron5-hybrid-8b`, `nemotron5-hybrid-56b` and `hf://` did not set it, so they inherited `apply_rope_fusion` from args ([base](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ae63ce48d2f0044170d828f658c3dd29dd0e4c98/examples/multimodal/config.py)).
  - They now always run without rope fusion. This is a performance-only effect, and only where those models use RoPE.

**Correction**
- This is main #6332's plumbing, so fix it on main and let the next sync bring it in, rather than diverging here.
- Make both flags switchable. Add `import argparse` at the top of the file, then:
  ```python
  group.add_argument(
      "--enable-fusions", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=True,
      help="Enable fusions in the model.",
  )
  ```
  Do the same for `--optimize-broadcast`. This keeps `--enable-fusions` and adds `--no-enable-fusions`.
- Add a TODO naming the follow-up that wires `args.enable_fusions` into the three `get_*_config` calls in `model_provider`.
- **Invariant:** every new flag has a reachable `False` state, plus either a reader or a TODO naming its consumer.
- When the wiring lands, choose the effective default deliberately. Passing `enable_fusions=args.enable_fusions` with today's default of `True` would turn on bias, dropout and rope fusions for every existing launch script.

**Preservation**
- Keep every flag name and the `True` default, so existing launch scripts that pass `--enable-fusions` or `--optimize-broadcast` still parse.
- Until consumers are wired, keep today's fusion-off configs: `enable_fusions=False` in all three config functions.

**Acceptance**
- *Proposed test:*
  - parsing `[]` gives `args.enable_fusions is True`;
  - `['--enable-fusions']` gives `True`;
  - `['--no-enable-fusions']` gives `False`;
  - repeat the same three cases for `--optimize-broadcast`.
- *Static check:* every `enable_fusions` or `optimize_broadcast` reference in `examples/multimodal/` is either a reader or sits next to a TODO naming its consumer.

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=low -->

## Review: nightly `main`→`dev` sync (2026-10-10), head `4236407f`

**Summary: 0 CRITICAL, 0 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION.** I found nothing that blocks this PR in the files I inspected. I am leaving a **comment rather than an approval** because my review did not cover the whole PR. Of the 373 changed files, 305 were left out of the inline diff. I looked closely at the risk areas specific to this sync and at the repair commit. Most of the omitted `megatron/core` source files and tests have not been reviewed yet (see *Coverage* below).

### Checked against the head and found correct

**Symmetric-memory fallback in the repair commit (behaviour change).**
- `FsdpParameterGroup` sets a flag on the partial-gradient buffer when [`allocate_partial_grad_buffer`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4236407f9d6f3e66dee178e57a1f701be00cd33c/megatron/core/distributed/fsdp/src/megatron_fsdp/experimental/parameter_group.py) allocates it.
- `DBuffer.reduce_scatter` uses `symm_mem.is_symm_mem_tensor` when that function exists. Otherwise it reads the flag, which defaults to `False` on the class.
- On torch builds without the detector, an ordinary AVG reduce-scatter is still tested by `test_partial_reduce_scatter_to_flat_average_without_symm_mem_detector` ([`test_dbuffer.py` L484-501](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/4236407f9d6f3e66dee178e57a1f701be00cd33c/tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2/test_dbuffer.py#L484-L501)).
- The two tests that call the detector directly are skipped through `requires_symm_mem_detector`.
